faqs.a:
(a)
Hearing Officer.
The authority shall consist of a sole hearing officer. The hearing officer may be
               chosen by the city clerk from any of the city's appointed judges as described in article
               III of
chapter 58
of this Code. While only one hearing officer shall preside over any meeting of the
               authority, the city clerk may select the hearing officer for any meeting from the
               pool of appointed judges.
(b)
Qualifications.
In addition to being a judge appointed pursuant to article III of
chapter 58
of this Code, a hearing officer must be an attorney currently licensed to practice
               in the State and be in good standing with the Supreme Court of the State. The hearing
               officer or any person in the hearing officer's immediate family must not have any
               financial interest in a liquor licensed establishment within the city. Ownership of
               stock solely for investment purposes in a corporation whose stock is publicly traded
               shall not be deemed to be a disqualifying financial interest.
(1)
For purposes of this section, "immediate family" means the hearing officer's spouse
               or person who identifies as their significant other or domestic partner and whose
               primary residence or place of primary abode is the same as that of the hearing officer.
               It also means the hearing officer's child, parent, sibling, aunt, uncle, or cousin,
               including biological, step, adopted foster, or in-law relationships.
(
Ord. No. 4670
, § 1, 12-17-2018;
Ord. No. 4872
, § 2, 4-15-2024)
State Law reference—
Local licensing authority as to fermented malt beverages, C.R.S. § 44-4-103; local
               licensing authority as to alcoholic beverages, C.R.S. § 44-3-135 et seq.
